hero.lead: A nation of 2.3 million on the Adriatic whose power is almost all renewable, with €922.1 million earmarked under the EU Growth Plan and €212.8 million already received.

capital.heading: Paid for every reform, and food for every table.

record.text: Available to Albania in total from the EU Reform and Growth Facility for the Western Balkans, to 2027
Released to Albania under the Growth Plan by 20 May 2026, after its third request for payment
General government gross debt, share of GDP, 2025

register.name: Eurobond due 2035
register.detail: Republic of Albania · coupon 4.75% · matures 14 February 2035
register.note: Issued in February 2025; one of four Eurobonds outstanding in the Ministry of Finance table of March 2026
register.text: A euro bond of the Republic of Albania sold to international investors, with a coupon of 4.75% and maturity on 14 February 2035. It is the newest of the four Eurobonds the Ministry of Finance lists as outstanding, and it finances the state budget.

register.name: Western Balkans Trade and Transport Facilitation 2.0, Phase II (Albania)
register.detail: World Bank · P514860 · approved 30 June 2026
register.note: The Albanian operation in a regional programme for the Western Balkans
register.text: The Albanian operation in the second phase of the World Bank’s Western Balkans Trade and Transport Facilitation programme, approved on 30 June 2026 with a principal of US$33.35 million. It serves the livelihood standard through trade and transport.

register.name: Improving Equitable Access to High Standard Public Services through GovTech, additional financing
register.detail: World Bank · P177845 · additional financing approved 10 March 2025
register.note: At least a 25% increase in online applications for public services projected
register.text: Additional financing to digitalise local government services and to build a new digital public procurement platform and a new system for managing public finances. The programme it expands also funds Youth Innovation Centers and 200 education SmartLabs in primary schools, which serve the education standard.

register.name: Second Resilience and Green Development DPL
register.detail: World Bank · P180679 · approved 12 February 2025 · second in a two-operation series
register.note: Budget support, the second of two operations
register.text: Budget support for the resilience of government and households, for a stronger energy market with more renewable energy and energy efficiency, and for protecting the environment. It serves the energy standard and the public finances behind all seven.

register.name: Clean and Resilient Environment for Blue Sea
register.detail: World Bank · P176163 · approved 1 December 2023
register.text: A World Bank loan for a cleaner and more resilient environment along Albania’s sea and coast, approved on 1 December 2023. It serves the livelihood standard on the coast, where visitors bring in a large share of export earnings.
register.note: Shown as Approved on the World Bank’s Finances One page, data as of 31 August 2026

register.name: First Resilience and Green Development DPL
register.detail: World Bank · P178202 · approved 16 March 2023 · first of two operations
register.text: Budget support for resilience and green growth, the first of a two-operation series. It serves the energy standard and the public finances behind all seven.
register.note: The second operation, also $120 million, was approved on 12 February 2025

register.name: Reform and Growth Facility (EU Growth Plan)
register.detail: European Commission · Reform Agenda approved October 2024 · €64.5 million pre-financing, March 2025 · €99.3 million, October 2025 · €49 million, 20 May 2026
register.text: Grants and concessional loans paid against the reforms in Albania’s Reform Agenda, part to the state budget and part to investment projects through the Western Balkans Investment Framework. The third release, €49 million on 20 May 2026, followed reforms in business competitiveness and innovation.
register.note: €212.8 million released to Albania by 20 May 2026

register.name: Underground substation in central Tirana
register.detail: EBRD · sovereign loan agreement with OSHEE · EBRD news of 1 April 2026 · 110/20 kV
register.note: Replaces €14.5 million from an earlier EBRD facility and adds €8 million
register.text: A sovereign loan to OSHEE, Albania’s state-owned electricity distribution and supply company, to build a new 110/20 kV underground substation in central Tirana. It makes the capital’s power network more reliable and serves the energy standard.

register.name: Municipal infrastructure works on the Gate to Alps
register.detail: EIB Global · framework loan to the Republic of Albania · signed 30 January 2026 · promoter Albanian Development Fund · total cost €100 million
register.note: With a €1.75 million technical assistance grant from the EIB’s Economic Resilience Initiative
register.text: A multisector framework loan for Shkodër, Lezhë and Malësi e Madhe in northern Albania: regional roads, public transport, water supply and sewerage, urban spaces, and natural and historical sites. It serves the water and livelihood standards.

register.name: 50 MWp solar power plant, KESH
register.detail: EBRD · sovereign guaranteed loan to KESH · EBRD news of 23 July 2025 · with an EU investment grant of up to €8 million and up to €1.2 million of technical assistance (WBIF)
register.note: Part of a package of up to €39.2 million with the EU
register.text: Finances a 50 MWp solar photovoltaic plant for KESH, the state-owned utility that produces almost 65% of Albania’s electricity, expected to generate over 70 GWh of renewable energy a year. It diversifies a power system that rests mostly on hydropower and serves the energy standard.

register.name: Durrës–Rrogozhina railway
register.detail: EIB Global and EU · signed 8 April 2025 · €30 million EIB loan · €60.5 million EU grant (WBIF) · €30 million co-financing from the EBRD
register.note: The EU financial package; total project cost about €121 million
register.text: Modernises the 34 km railway between Durrës and Rrogozhina in central Albania, under an agreement signed with the Ministry of Infrastructure and Energy. It serves the livelihood standard through transport.

register.name: Vorë–Hani i Hotit railway
register.detail: EIB Global · signed 20 March 2024 · with an approved €126 million EU investment grant (WBIF) and a €98.75 million EBRD loan · 120 km
register.note: The EIB loan; the EU grant and the EBRD loan are alongside
register.text: Modernises and electrifies the 120 km railway from Vorë to Hani i Hotit, with 12 rebuilt stations and new signalling, for speeds of up to 120 km/h. It serves the livelihood standard through transport.

register.name: Rehabilitation of the Fierza hydropower plant
register.detail: KfW loan · WBIF grant WB-IG05-ALB-ENE-01 of €8,722,449 · EU Economic and Investment Plan, Flagship 4
register.note: WBIF stage: tender preparation; the Newswire reports Parliament’s approval of the loan in March 2026
register.text: Rehabilitates the electro-mechanical components and supporting network of the Fierza hydropower plant, to extend its operating life by at least 30 years and raise its output by 10%. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: SME portfolio guarantee, ProCredit Bank Albania
register.detail: EBRD · EU first-loss cover through EFSD+, Growth4All programme · EU Delegation to Albania, 15 July 2026 · covers 50% of the credit risk
register.note: Up to €50 million in new lending to Albanian SMEs
register.text: An unfunded guarantee on a new portfolio of loans to small and medium-sized firms, focused on businesses led or owned by women and young entrepreneurs; half of the guaranteed share goes to green investments. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Loan for innovative and green SMEs, Intesa Sanpaolo Bank Albania
register.detail: EIB · signed 11 May 2026 · first credit line under the EU’s Innovation and Green Transformation Facility for the Western Balkans
register.note: Blended credit line for SMEs and mid-caps
register.text: A credit line for small and medium-sized firms and mid-caps to invest in innovation, digitalisation, climate action and environmental sustainability. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: SME portfolio guarantee, Union Bank
register.detail: EBRD · EU first-loss cover of up to €2.5 million through EFSD+ · EBRD news, 2026 · covers up to 50% of the credit risk
register.note: On a new SME loan portfolio of up to €50 million; at least 30% for green projects
register.text: An unfunded portfolio guarantee to Union Bank, a commercial bank specialised in SME and retail lending, to expand lending to small and medium-sized firms, including green projects, and advance financial inclusion. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Loans for Roma entrepreneurs through REDI
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved 20 November 2025 · €5 million loan to REDI Economic Development SA, Luxembourg · Albania, Kosovo, the Republic of Moldova and Romania
register.note: €5 million for four countries; the share of Albania is not stated
register.text: On-lends through partner microfinance institutions to Roma entrepreneurs, with at least 30% expected for women, and pairs credit with financial literacy and business support from REDI NGO. It is expected to sustain or create about 2,000 jobs across the four countries and serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Green loan, ProCredit Bank Albania (WB GOLD)
register.detail: EBRD · Western Balkans Green Outcomes-Linked Debt Financing Framework · EBRD news, 2025 · first WB GOLD transaction in Albania
register.note: At least half for green transition projects
register.text: A loan for on-lending to small and mid-sized businesses and mid-caps, with outcome-based incentives for investment in energy-efficient technologies and renewable energy. It serves the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Loan to FED Invest for vulnerable groups
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved 5 April 2025 · guarantee from the CEB’s Social Impact Account · €49,000 technical assistance grant from the Slovak Inclusive Growth Account
register.note: At least 35% for women entrepreneurs; 3,000 micro-enterprises and farms and at least 250 jobs expected
register.text: Supports employment and income-generating activities for vulnerable groups throughout Albania through the microfinance institution FED Invest, with financial literacy services for rural residents, including women. It serves the livelihood and food standards.

register.name: Green loan facility to Fondi BESA
register.detail: responsAbility, Climate Finance strategy · announced 11 February 2026 · senior unsecured · two facilities of €6 million · the first disbursed in mid-December 2025
register.note: For energy-efficiency home improvements and small solar PV systems
register.text: A green loan facility to Albania’s largest regulated non-banking microfinance institution, to grow its lending for energy-efficiency home improvements and small-scale solar photovoltaic systems for households and small firms. It serves the energy and shelter standards.

register.name: Loan to NOA
register.detail: Grameen Crédit Agricole Foundation · partner since 2024
register.note: NOA serves 17,683 beneficiaries, 35.7% of them women
register.text: A loan to NOA, a microfinance institution established in 1998 by USAID that provides credit, technical support and payments to Albanian entrepreneurs, farmers and families. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Loan to Agro & Social Fund
register.detail: Grameen Crédit Agricole Foundation · partner since 2024 · in local currency
register.note: Agro & Social Fund serves 3,720 beneficiaries, 54.2% of them rural
register.text: A loan to Agro & Social Fund, a microfinance institution set up in 2001 by World Vision Albania that finances farmers and rural micro-entrepreneurs. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2011
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2020
items.text: Visitors already pay for the coast and the culture; their spending can finance what lasts.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2025
items.text: Citizens abroad send home a steady share of the economy: a flow that can back long-term finance.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 16.6% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Fondi BESA
items.text: Albania’s largest regulated non-banking microfinance institution, which served approximately 27,500 MSME clients nationwide in mid-2025. A green loan facility from responsAbility, announced in February 2026, finances energy-efficiency home improvements and small-scale solar PV systems for households and small firms.

items.name: Albaponik
items.text: A hydroponic farm in the hills of Baldushk near Tirana that grows leafy greens and herbs in nutrient-enriched water instead of soil, with zero pesticides and herbicides, on over 3,000 square metres. Its recirculating system reduces water usage by up to 90% compared to traditional farming.

items.name: Agro & Social Fund
items.text: A microfinance institution set up in 2001 by World Vision Albania, specialising in credit for farming, with products designed around farming seasons and the needs of small family farms. It serves 3,720 beneficiaries, 43.9% of them women and 54.2% rural.

items.name: Psikologu Online
items.text: Albania’s first platform of its kind, established in 2021, offering competitively priced online psychological consultations and free psychoeducational resources to Albanian speakers, including those with limited access to mental health services. It reports 40–70 new monthly clients receiving professional therapy.

items.name: FED Invest
items.text: A microfinance institution that lends for employment and income-generating activities of vulnerable groups throughout Albania. A €10 million loan approved by the Council of Europe Development Bank in April 2025, with at least 35% for women entrepreneurs, is expected to assist 3,000 micro-enterprises and farms.

items.name: Crystal Team
items.text: A social enterprise in Berat specialising in professional cleaning, established to give women from the Roma and Egyptian communities meaningful employment. It is supported by the Challenge Fund of the EU4Innovation project.
